chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'When the water in the well is a Kurr, nothing will pollute it.'
I said: 'And how much is a Kurr?' He said: 'Three and a half spans in depth by three and a half spans in width.'

key_terms.أَشْبَار: Spans (plural of shibr) — a traditional unit of length measured by the width of an open hand
key_terms.الرَّكِيّ: Well or cistern (used for ritual purification water)
key_terms.كُرّ: Kurr — a unit of water volume in Islamic law; water that meets or exceeds this threshold cannot be made impure by contact with najasah
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْ: To render impure (najis) — the technical jurisprudential term for ritual pollution

ai.seo_question: What is the volume of a Kurr of water according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the legal threshold for water purity: a well containing at least one Kurr of water cannot be rendered impure by external contaminants. The Kurr is defined as a cube measuring three and a half hand-spans in each dimension — depth and width. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining when well water retains its purity despite contact with najasah (ritual impurity).
